Core Pillar 02 • Studio Engineering & Production Dossier

Behind the Scenes on Music Generation

At Engine Room Records, artificial intelligence is never treated as a “push-button replacement” for human storytelling. Every album is a multi-stage studio collaboration combining Michael P. Ragsdale's personal narrative concepts, libretto co-writing with Google Gemini, iterative vocal and acoustic engineering in Suno v5 / v6, and local mastering via our automated Harper Audio Engine.

🎧 Hear The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ in The Listening Room ↗ 🎛️ Listen to Starfield Calibration (2011 / 2026) ↗
Stage 01–04 • End-to-End Studio Workflow

1. The 4-Stage Human + AI Production Architecture

Stage 1: Human Narrative Architecture & Libretto

Every song starts in the Markdown narrative archives (books.raggiesoft.com). Before a single note is rendered, we establish who is singing, why the song exists in-universe (such as Cassidy finding safety in Ryan's embrace on Echoes in the Wire, or the Rowlands siblings broadcasting Upon This Winter's Night across the Appalachian mountains for Julian), and its exact tempo, key feel, and structural cues.

Stage 2: Acoustic & Phonetic Vowel Extensions

Standard written prose often produces clipped or rushed vocal synthesis on long melodic sustains. To engineer soaring 1980s stadium belts and zero-gravity harmonic tails, our librettos embed explicit phonetic vowel extensions (ooh, aah, ee, oh) and breath-cadence markers directly into the studio lyric sheets. In-universe on Starfield Calibration, these lyrical evolutions celebrate the band's freedom from Apex Records alongside Cassidy's open-room acoustic phrasing.

Stage 3: Suno v5 / v6 Generation & 75% Cover Calibration

Tracks are generated under a paid commercial Suno subscription (granting 100% commercial ownership to Michael P. Ragsdale). When upgrading legacy recordings into our signature 2011 remaster suite (Starfield Calibration) or live stadium arrangements, we use the 75% Cover Audio Influence Protocol—preserving the core melody and sibling vocal chemistry while rebuilding the instrumentation with wide-field analog space-synth or stadium separation.

Stage 4: Google Gemini Multimodal WebVTT & Harper CC BY-SA 4.0 Mastering

Once a master WAV passes human quality review, Google Gemini listens directly to the rendered audio alongside the studio lyric sheet to author a frame-accurate SYNC_TYPE: HUMAN_VERIFIED WebVTT (.vtt) timed lyric file. Our local Harper Audio Engine (harper.sh) then transcodes the master into 128kbps web preview MP3s and free CC BY-SA 4.0 ZIP archives (bundling /lyrics/, /metadata/, and each song's /suno-prompts/ markdown file so fellow creators know how to recreate every track), while keeping uncompressed WAV/FLAC masters isolated inside our local /raggiesoft-vaults sanctuary.

Acoustic Discovery • The 75% Benchmark

2. Why Lyrical & Sonic Changes Happened on Starfield Calibration

Listeners comparing original 1987–1997 releases (such as Electric Color, Neon Hearts, and Hard Reset) against the 2011 Starfield Calibration Cosmic Tidal Lock mixes will notice intentional lyrical and vocal phrasing updates. Both the in-universe and studio reasons are one and the same:

  1. Celebrating Emancipation from Apex Records: In-universe, Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler reclaimed their early 1980s songs from Apex Records' suffocating corporate pop template, rewriting coerced lines into an unapologetic celebration of family autonomy. Notably, Echoes in the Wire (and its Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix) permanently replaced Apex's coerced 1989 ballad If You Walked Away—transforming a song of manufactured heartbreak into the true story of Cassidy finding comfort and safety when her brother Ryan is hugging her tightly.
  2. Acoustic & Phonetic Vowel Extensions: By opening cramped syllables into resonant vowel sustains (ooh, aah, ee, oh) and pairing them with our 75% Cover Audio Influence calibration, the vocal harmonies lock into synchronous phase with Cassidy's analog synthesizer pads.
Intellectual Property & Open Culture

3. Open-Culture Trademark Policy & Dual Timeline Specification

Proprietary Brand Mark vs. Open Genre

The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ is the proprietary brand mark identifying works produced by Engine Room Records and The Stardust Engine. However, we believe musical genres belong to everyone: the descriptive genre term “80s Cosmic Pop” is intentionally dedicated to the open creative commons so any artist, producer, or fan can freely tag and create music in that style.

Dual Timeline Policy & Zero-Numbers DSP Artwork

Every release carries two explicit ISO 8601 dates in its Schema.org metadata: temporalCoverage (the in-universe lore year, e.g., 1987 for Electric Color or 2004-09-21 for Progress Street) and datePublished (the real-world 2026 production year). To comply with strict Apple Music and Spotify cover-art inspection rules, all 1:1 album covers contain zero numbers or dates, featuring only the artist name and album title.

Engine Room Records (Real-World Imprint)

In real life, Engine Room Records (never “Engine Room Records, LLC”) is the creative brand and private record imprint under which Michael P. Ragsdale produces and distributes his music.
